IS J 3053 -1977 

Indian Standard 

SPECIFICATION FOR 
CANE BASKETS FOR GENERAL PURPOSES 

(First Revision) 



0, FOREWORD 

0.1 This Indian Standard ( First Revision ) was adopted by the Indian 
Standards Institution on !3 April 1977, after the draft finalized by the 
Timber Stores Sectional Committee had been approved by the Civil 
Engineering Division Council. 

0.2 Large quantities of cane baskets of various sizes and designs are used 
by the Indian Railways, defence services, coal mines and several other 
organizations for general purposes. As the demand for cane ( rattans ) 
is increasing day by day and the supply is not adequate, this standard 
has been prepared with the object of limiting the sizes and indicating 
design of cane baskets with a view to affecting maximum economy in the 
use of canes for such baskets. 

0.2.1 This standard was originally published in 1965. During the course 
of working to the standard some difnculties have been experienced regard- 
ing the provisions relating to the manufacture of these baskets and, 
therefore, in this revision, these provisions have been suitably reworded 
to clarify the provisions. 

0.3 This standard contains clause 4.1.1 which calls for agreement between 
the manufacturer and the purchaser. 

0.4 In the formulation of this standard due weightage has been given to 
international co-ordination among the standards and practices prevail- 
ing in different countries in addition to relating it to the practices in the 
field in this country. 

0.5 For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this 
standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, express- 
ing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance 
with IS: 2-1960*. The number of significant places retained in the 
rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in 
this standard. 



*Rules for rounding off numerical values ( revised ). 



18:3053-1977 

1. SCOPE 

1.1 This standard covers the essential requirements for cane baskets used 
for general purposes. 

2. TERMINOLOGY 

2.0 For the purpose of this standard, the following definitions shall apply. 

2.1 Immatare Cane — Cane, which discolours readily, is brittle and 

shrinks badly. 

2.2 Banding — Working a single weaver in front and behind alternate 

stakes. 

2.3 Stakes — The rods which form the upright in the sides of the basket. 

2.4 Weaver ( Randing ) — Weaver is a rod which is worked in randing 
the basket. 

3. CANES ( RATTANS ) SUITABLE FOR BASKETS 

3.1 The baskets shall be manufactured from any species of canes (rattan). 

3.2 The cane shall be mature, clean, free from any kind of decay ( rot ) 
and insect attack. The whole cane, before manufacture, shall be capable 
of being bent to a circle of a diameter of 150 mm without showing any 
signs of fracture. This test shall be carried out after conditioning 
the cane for a period of approximately 96 hours at 27 =fc 2°G and 
relative humidity 65 ± 2 percent. 

3.3 The diameter of cane for stakes and weavers, for sizes 1 and 2 
baskets ( see 4.1 ) shall be 9 ± 3 mm. However, for sizes 3 and 4 baskets, 
the diameter of cane for stakes and weavers shall be 12 =fc 3 mm except 
that the first ten rounds ( weavers ) from the bottom may be of 9 ± 3 mm 
diameter, 

4. SIZES AND TOLERANCES 

4.1 Sizes — The cane baskets shall be of the following nominal sizes ;

5. C<»^STRUG1^0^ 

5.1 The foundation of the basket shall b^for^ied by four sets of stakes; 
three sets haying four st^l^ea q^ch an^^ the fp>?rii| one haying three stakes 
only. T^wp of the sets haying fb^r stakes, eaph shajl be laid at right 
angles to each other and the other two cro$3-wise in the angles^thus 
formed. The diameter of the central tie shall not exceed 150 mni. The 
ends of the stakes shall be woven into the border of the basket and pushed 
down between the weavers to a distance of at least 75 mm. The method 
of weaving shall be as indicated in Fig. 1. The randing of the basket 
shall be as close as possible and all ends shall be trimmed and finished on 
the inside of the basket. 

5.2 The basket shall be strengthened with 2 steel strips of 20 =fc 2 mm 
width and 1*00 ± 0'16 mm thickness ( see IS : 1029-1970* ). These shall 
pass from one edge of the basket to the other, through the bottom of the 
basket and approximately at right angles to each other. The strips shall 
be bent over at the edges for not less than 100 mm and securely fastened. 

6. WORKMANSHIP AND FINISH 

6.1 The baskets shall be well made and tightly woven. The general 
workmanship and finish shall be reasonably good. 

7. SAMPLING 

7.1 Unless otherwise agreed to between the supplier and the purchaser, 
IS: 2500 ( Part I )-1973t, shall be followed for sampling inspection for 
determining acceptability or otherwise of a lot to the requirements of 
this specification. The inspection level and sampling plan as given 
in 7.1.1 and 7.1.2 shall be followed. 

7.1.1 The scale of sampling shall be corresponding to inspection 
level III given in Table 1 of IS : 2500 ( Part I )-1973t. 

7.1.2 The sampling plan to be followed shall be single sampling plan 
corresponding to acceptable quality level (AQL) value of 4*0 percent 
given in Table 2 of IS : 2500 (Part I)-1973t. 

8. MARKING 

8.1 Unless otherwise specified, a metallic label, approximately 75 X 50 mm, 
marked with the manufacturer's name or initials or recognized trade- 
mark, the year of manufacture and the size of the basket ( 1, 2, 3 or 4) 
( see 4.1 ) shall be tied to each basket by means of a wire.

8.1.1 The basket may also be marked with the ISI Certification Mark. 

Note — The use of the ISI Certification Mark is governed by the provisions of the 
Indian Standards Institution ( Certification Marks ) Act and the Rules and 
Regulations made thereunder. The ISI Mark on products covered by an Indian 
Standard conveys the assurance that they have been produced to comply with the 
requirements of that standard under a well-defined system of inspection, testing and 
quality control v/hJch is devised and supervised by ISI and operated by the producer. 
ISI marked products are also continuously checked by ISI for conformity to that 
standard as a fur^Jber attifeguard. Details of conditions under which a licence for the 
use of the ISI CciaificAtion Mark may be granted to manufacturers or processors may 
be obtained from the Indian Standards Institution.
